hook: I sprinted the last hill. Why did my next run feel worse?
source_problem: I pushed the last climb much harder than planned and carried it into the next day.
exact_reddit_language: I pushed the last climb much harder than planned and carried it into the next day.
emotion: proud for one minute, regretful the next day

hook_source.why_it_works: A concrete problem, recognizable moment, and clear payoff.

hook_quality.rationale: 62/70; 12 words; bank family marathon_last_hill_sprint_v1; pain 9/10; curiosity 10/10; simplicity 8/10; passes quality gate

cta: Follow the next workout, including the bad decisions.

character_anchor.identity_prompt: photorealistic fictional adult female beginner runner, late 20s to early 30s, realistic non-elite beginner build, natural warm face, brown hair tied back, relatable marathon-training journey energy, realistic sweat, modest simple technical running kit, visible Apple Watch-style or Garmin-style running watch on one wrist, real outdoor running moment
character_anchor.brand_anchor_prompt: photorealistic fictional female beginner runner training for a marathon, realistic beginner build, natural face, brown hair tied back, modest simple technical running kit, visible Apple Watch-style or Garmin-style running watch on one wrist, honest running effort, tired-but-happy post-workout satisfaction when appropriate, selected forest/mountain/lake route world, believable TikTok-native marathon journal aesthetic
character_anchor.reference_instruction: Use only the Road to Marathon Fit female-runner reference as the identity reference. Do not use or imitate the main Coachi male runner, the Runner Watch Lab male runner, their faces, body types, poses, or original backgrounds.
stable_traits: use the Road to Marathon Fit female runner identity for the marathon account

character_anchor.variation_policy: Use this as the Road to Marathon Fit avatar: a fictional female beginner runner starting a six-month marathon build. She should sometimes look tired, sweaty, and post-workout happy or satisfied, not always polished. Keep body changes subtle over time; do not create dramatic transformation claims. Rotate forest, mountain, and lake worlds; rotate pre-workout, during-workout, and post-workout moments; keep the runner relatable, modest, and training-focused. Do not use the main Coachi male runner or Runner Watch Lab male runner as style, face, body, pose, or age reference.
character_anchor.watch_rule: Use the selected visible watch type naturally on one wrist. The watch may read as Apple Watch-style or Garmin-style by silhouette only. Keep it small and believable in-frame. No readable screen UI, no logo, no wrist close-up, and no watch-checking pose.

schema_prompt_template: same runner on {route}, realistic steady jog, clean negative space for headline, natural light
production_rules: Every slideshow has an explicit emotion, one Images 2.0 hook, one generated avatar world, and one final CTA.
Slide hook and slides 1-6 should use the source-backed TikTok slideshow text bank before any generic AI wording.
Do not generate all slideshow images in one Images 2.0 request.
Do not bake overlay text into the image.
Keep the full deck in one visual world and one lighting family.
For the hook image, reference-image background is non-transferable; the generated background must match visual_world.
Keep one primary visual world per slideshow; lake worlds may include mountains or hills as background context.
Use Supabase/curated library assets for slides 2 through the CTA slide.
Composite all text locally with Sharp/Canvas.
